children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you find out if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you a few questions about your circumstances.

Let's start with the basics:

**How many children are you looking to claim Child Benefit for, and what are their names and ages?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! I'm looking to claim for my son Alex. He's 8 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! It's great to meet you (and Alex, in a sense!).

Now, let me ask a few more questions to assess your eligibility:

**Are you responsible for Alex? This typically means he lives with you, or you contribute at least the same amount as Child Benefit towards his upkeep each week (currently £25.60 for an eldest or only child).**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, he lives with me. Well, actually, he's been in the hospital for a few months now. But he's still my son and lives with me when he's not there.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I'm sorry to hear Alex has been in the hospital – I hope he's recovering well.

Thank you for sharing that. Before I continue, let me check the specific rules around children who are in hospital to make sure I give you accurate information.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for your patience. I can see from the guidance that hospital stays can affect Child Benefit, but there are important details I need to clarify.

**You mentioned Alex has been in hospital for "a few months" – could you tell me approximately how long he has been in hospital? Specifically, has it been more or less than 12 weeks?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: It's been about 15 weeks now, so yes, more than 12 weeks.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. Since Alex has been in hospital for more than 12 weeks, there's an important exception that could still allow you to receive Child Benefit.

**Do you regularly spend money on Alex while he's in hospital?** This could include things like visiting him (travel costs), bringing him items, clothes, treats, or other expenses related to his care and comfort.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, I haven't really been able to afford to spend money on him while he's been in there. It's been difficult financially.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I understand – financial difficulties can make things really tough, and I'm sorry to hear you're going through that.

I have just a couple more questions to complete my assessment:

**Do you live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for confirming that.

One final question:

**Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex, or has anyone else been looking after him?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, no one else is claiming Child Benefit for him. He's my son and I'm the one responsible for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing all that information. I now have everything I need to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

Based on the information you've shared, I'm afraid I have some difficult news to deliver.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I'm sorry to say that based on the information you've provided, **you are not currently eligible for Child Benefit for Alex**.

Here's why:

- Under normal circumstances, you would qualify for Child Benefit as you live in the UK, Alex is under 16, and he normally lives with you.
- However, because Alex has been in hospital for more than 12 weeks (approximately 15 weeks), Child Benefit entitlement typically stops after this time limit.
- There is an exception that allows you to continue receiving Child Benefit if you are **regularly spending money** on Alex while he's in hospital – but since you've mentioned you haven't been able to afford to do so, this exception doesn't apply.

**What you can do:**
- If your circumstances change and you begin regularly spending money on Alex while he's in hospital, you may become eligible again. I'd recommend contacting the Child Benefit Office to discuss your situation.
- Once Alex is discharged from hospital and comes home to live with you, you should be able to claim Child Benefit for him again.

I'm truly sorry this isn't better news, especially given the difficult time you're going through. I hope Alex recovers soon and is able to come home.

However, the claimant has confirmed they have not been able to afford to regularly spend money on Alex while he's been in hospital. Since the 12-week limit has been exceeded and the exception (regularly spending money on the child) does not apply, the claimant is not currently eligible for Child Benefit for Alex.
